items.name: Brionna Jones
items.short_comment: General manager Dan Padover said Friday that Jones (leg) won't return to game action before the FIBA World Cup break, Meghan L. Hall of USA Today reports.
items.long_comment: Padover added that the team hopes to provide an update on Jones after the break. Madina Okot will likely continue to see a slight bump in minutes behind Angel Reese until Jones is cleared to play.

items.name: Skylar Diggins
items.short_comment: Diggins (knee) will miss the remainder of the 2026 WNBA season, Sara Jane Gamelli of BallisLife.com reports.
items.long_comment: She will now "focus on recovering an aggravated right knee injury." She hadn't played since July 3 and her rehab didn't progress as quickly as she would've hoped. She appeared in 19 games and posted averages of 14.2 points, 3.2 rebounds and 4.9 assists.

items.name: Rickea Jackson
items.short_comment: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.
items.long_comment: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.

items.name: Leila Lacan
items.short_comment: The Sun announced Sunday that Lacan will join Team France for the FIBA World Cup and miss the Sun's next four games.
items.long_comment: Lacan will report to Team France early after averaging 11.6 points, 4.6 assists, 1.9 rebounds and 1.7 steals across 28.4 minutes per game in her first 27 regular-season appearances this year. Charlisse Leger-Walker, Saniya Rivers and Hailey Van Lith could all see increased playing time in Lacan's stead.

items.name: Azzi Fudd
items.short_comment: Fudd will undergo an arthroscopic procedure to address her right knee soreness and will be sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 season.
items.long_comment: Fudd has been sidelined since early August due to her ongoing right knee soreness, and she'll undergo a procedure that will ultimately end her rookie season. Across 30 regular-season appearances (24 starts) this year, she averaged 13.1 points, 1.8 assists, 1.7 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 31.7 minutes per game. In her absence, Odyssey Sims, Alanna Smith and Alysha Clark have seen increased roles, and that trend will likely continue down the stretch as the Wings compete for a playoff berth.

items.name: Costanza Verona
items.short_comment: Verona's contract was temporarily suspended by the Wings Saturday.
items.long_comment: Verona is signed to a developmental contract, so she has only appeared in one regular-season game for Dallas during the 2026 campaign. She will now head overseas, where she will suit up for the Italian National Team for the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup. It's unknown whether Verona will be back with the Wings, though her departure will allow the team to sign another player to a developmental deal.

items.name: Gabby Williams
items.short_comment: Williams (not injury related) finished with 25 points (8-12 FG, 6-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, four assists and two steals across 18 minutes in France's 111-56 FIBA World Cup win over Nigeria on Monday.
items.long_comment: Williams torched the nets for France on Monday, leading all players in scoring and triples made while pacing her team in rebounds. The 29-year-old scored at least 14 points in all three of her group phase appearances, and she'll now turn her focus to the quarterfinals Thursday, when France will face the winner of Wednesday's matchup between Puerto Rico and China. Williams had her contract temporarily suspended ahead of the World Cup, and her next chance to play for the Valkyries will come versus Portland on Sept. 18.

items.name: Cecilia Zandalasini
items.short_comment: Zandalasini finished with 14 points (5-14 FG, 1-7 3Pt, 3-5 FT) and seven rebounds over 26 minutes in Italy's 55-52 FIBA World Cup loss to USA on Sunday.
items.long_comment: Italy came close to earning the win, with Zandalasini being the only member of her team to reach double figures in scoring. However, despite ending with a game high in points Sunday, she wasn't efficient and has now shot just 22.2 percent from behind the arc in the first two games of the 2026 FIBA World Cup.

items.name: Janelle Salaun
items.short_comment: Salaun registered seven points (3-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt) and seven rebounds in 24 minutes during Thursday's 79-60 win over New York.
items.long_comment: Salaun struggled to find the bottom of the net in this one, though she managed to contribute elsewhere by turning in her best rebounding night since July 10. She'll end her streak of double-digit scoring performances at five games following Thursday's showing. Salaun will now set her sights on the FIBA World Cup and is slated to miss Sunday's matchup against the Fire to head overseas. She's expected to return to the Valkyries in time for a Sept. 18 matchup against the Fire.

items.name: Iliana Rupert
items.short_comment: Rupert is pregnant, and the Valkyries have filed for a replacement contract ahead of the 2026 season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports Thursday.
items.long_comment: Rupert signed a multi-year contract with Golden State during the offseason and missed the start of training camp due to an overseas commitment. Her status for the 2026 regular season now appears to be in jeopardy due to her pregnancy. The 24-year-old made 21 regular-season appearances (11 starts) for the Valkyries last year and averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 23.1 minutes per game. If Rupert is sidelined in 2026, Janelle Salaun, Kiah Stokes and Laeticia Amihere are candidates to see increased work.

items.short_comment: The Aces announced Thursday that Smith will be sidelined for the rest of the season after suffering a non-contact left leg injury during Sunday's game versus the Tempo, per Chelsea Leite of TSN.
items.long_comment: It's a big blow for the defending-champion Aces ahead of the postseason. Smith started all 38 of her appearances for Las Vegas, so a spot in the first unit is now open. Brianna Turner appears to the most likely candidate to replace Smith in the starting lineup going forward.

items.long_comment: Juhasz didn't deliver her most efficient performance, though she was still one of four players to score in double figures for Hungary. She also finished third on the team in rebounds and assists. The 26-year-old forward and Hungary will now look toward their quarterfinals matchup with Team USA on Thursday.

items.short_comment: Nogic (not injury related) intends to play professionally in Russia and won't return to Phoenix this season, Aya Abdeen of TheIXSports.com reports.
items.long_comment: Nogic had her contract temporarily suspended June 20 and will now be out for the remainder of the WNBA season, as she's slated to compete overseas in Russia with an eye on leading the Serbian national team in the EuroBasket 2027 qualifiers. The guard appeared in 16 games (seven starts) for Phoenix, averaging 10.4 points, 1.6 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 20.2 minutes per contest. With Nogic out of the fold for the foreseeable future, Alexa Held stands to continue benefiting from expanded opportunities in the backcourt.

items.name: Frieda Buhner
items.short_comment: Buhner (not injury related) notched 21 points (7-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds and one assist across 20 minutes in Germany's 83-58 FIBA World Cup win over Mali on Monday.
items.long_comment: Buhner torched the nets from beyond the arc Monday, finishing as one of only two players to score in double figures for Germany. Although she didn't offer much outside the scoring column, the 22-year-old led all players in scoring. She had her contract temporarily suspended by the Fire ahead of the World Cup, and her next chance to play in the WNBA will come against Phoenix on Sept. 17. For now, Buhner and Germany will focus on Tuesday's game against Korea, during which the two sides will fight for the right to face Belgium in the quarterfinals Thursday.

items.name: Sarah Ashlee Barker
items.short_comment: The Fire announced Friday that Barker will undergo surgery to repair a torn ACL and will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign.
items.long_comment: Barker was helped to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's loss to the Wings, and she's now been diagnosed with a season-ending injury. The second-year guard took on a significant role for the Fire after the club selected her in the 2026 WNBA Expansion Draft. Across 26 regular-season games (15 starts), the 24-year-old averaged 10.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per contest. Karlie Samuelson, Teja Oblak and Nyadiew Puoch are candidates for increased playing time in Barker's stead.

items.short_comment: Feagin (knee) was diagnosed with a torn left ACL on Thursday and will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign, WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.
items.long_comment: Feagin agreed to a developmental contract with Portland on June 24 after spending time in Los Angeles. After appearing in 16 regular-season games for the Sparks in 2025, the 23-year-old played in only three regular-season contests in 2026, logging a combined 10 minutes. Feagin had yet to make her debut with the Fire, though that will now need to wait, assuming Portland keeps her on the roster moving ahead.

items.short_comment: The Storm announced Friday that Samuelson underwent successful left knee surgery and will miss the remainder of the season.
items.long_comment: Seattle's frontcourt takes another hit after losing Ezi Magbegor to a torn ACL on Thursday. Samuelson had a delayed start to the year due ACL surgery recovery, averaging 4.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 0.8 assists in 15.3 minutes per contest over 32 games this season. The Storm should lean more heavily on Stefanie Dolson, Mackenzie Holmes and Taylor Thierry the rest of the way.

items.short_comment: Fam (not injury related) generated 16 points (7-18 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and one steal across 27 minutes in Spain's 79-59 FIBA World Cup win over Japan on Monday.
items.long_comment: Although she didn't deliver her most efficient outing Monday, Fam still bounced back after scoring just four points on 2-of-7 shooting in Saturday's loss to Mali. The 20-year-old led Spain in rebounds and was the team's second-leading scorer, resulting in her lone double-double of the group phase. She had her contract temporarily suspended by the Storm ahead of the World Cup, and her next chance to play for the club will come against the Aces on Sept. 17. For now, Fam and Spain will prepare for the quarterfinals Thursday, when they'll face the winner of Wednesday's matchup between Italy and Australia.

availability.name: Katie Lou Samuelson
availability.short_comment: The Storm announced Friday that Samuelson underwent successful left knee surgery and will miss the remainder of the season.
availability.long_comment: Seattle's frontcourt takes another hit after losing Ezi Magbegor to a torn ACL on Thursday. Samuelson had a delayed start to the year due ACL surgery recovery, averaging 4.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 0.8 assists in 15.3 minutes per contest over 32 games this season. The Storm should lean more heavily on Stefanie Dolson, Mackenzie Holmes and Taylor Thierry the rest of the way.
availability.authority_note: ESPN injury feed. Status is ESPN’s; comment text often cites a named reporter. Not the league’s official injury report.

availability.name: Jade Melbourne
availability.short_comment: Melbourne (illness) didn't play in Thursday's 89-66 FIBA World Cup loss to Spain.
availability.long_comment: Melbourne was pulled early from Australia's previous matchup against Italy on Wednesday due to illness, and she evidently didn't feel healthy enough to give it a go Thursday. Australia has been eliminated, so Melbourne will turn her attention to getting back on the court in time for Seattle's upcoming game against Las Vegas on Sept. 17.

availability.name: Awa Fam
availability.short_comment: Fam (not injury related) generated 16 points (7-18 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and one steal across 27 minutes in Spain's 79-59 FIBA World Cup win over Japan on Monday.
availability.long_comment: Although she didn't deliver her most efficient outing Monday, Fam still bounced back after scoring just four points on 2-of-7 shooting in Saturday's loss to Mali. The 20-year-old led Spain in rebounds and was the team's second-leading scorer, resulting in her lone double-double of the group phase. She had her contract temporarily suspended by the Storm ahead of the World Cup, and her next chance to play for the club will come against the Aces on Sept. 17. For now, Fam and Spain will prepare for the quarterfinals Thursday, when they'll face the winner of Wednesday's matchup between Italy and Australia.
availability.authority_note: ESPN injury feed. Status is ESPN’s; comment text often cites a named reporter. Not the league’s official injury report.

availability.name: Natisha Hiedeman
availability.short_comment: Hiedeman (shoulder) won't play Sunday against the Sparks.
availability.long_comment: This will be Hiedeman's fourth consecutive game on the inactive list, and it's not a great sign that she continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff. For now, she should be considered questionable for Seattle's next game against Las Vegas on Sept. 17.

availability.name: Katie Lou Samuelson
availability.short_comment: The Storm announced Friday that Samuelson underwent successful left knee surgery and will miss the remainder of the season.
availability.long_comment: Seattle's frontcourt takes another hit after losing Ezi Magbegor to a torn ACL on Thursday. Samuelson had a delayed start to the year due ACL surgery recovery, averaging 4.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 0.8 assists in 15.3 minutes per contest over 32 games this season. The Storm should lean more heavily on Stefanie Dolson, Mackenzie Holmes and Taylor Thierry the rest of the way.

availability.name: Awa Fam
availability.short_comment: Fam (not injury related) generated 16 points (7-18 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), 10 rebounds, two assists and one steal across 27 minutes in Spain's 79-59 FIBA World Cup win over Japan on Monday.
availability.long_comment: Although she didn't deliver her most efficient outing Monday, Fam still bounced back after scoring just four points on 2-of-7 shooting in Saturday's loss to Mali. The 20-year-old led Spain in rebounds and was the team's second-leading scorer, resulting in her lone double-double of the group phase. She had her contract temporarily suspended by the Storm ahead of the World Cup, and her next chance to play for the club will come against the Aces on Sept. 17. For now, Fam and Spain will prepare for the quarterfinals Thursday, when they'll face the winner of Wednesday's matchup between Italy and Australia.

availability.name: Rickea Jackson
availability.short_comment: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.
availability.long_comment: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.
